disposition_reason: Summarizes 20,542 USDA residue-monitoring liver samples and prints mean total arsenic in young-chicken liver for 1994-2000 and selected years; muscle values are modeled.

study.design: Analysis of national residue monitoring data with exposure modeling
study.method: USDA FSIS National Residue Program total arsenic analysis (method not described in this paper)

findings.group: young chickens, USDA FSIS National Residue Program, 1994-2000
findings.reported: mean for the entire period was 0.39 ppm
findings.notes: Mean computed with non-quantifiable results (< 0.20 ppm) set to 0.10 ppm; 30% of young-chicken liver samples were non-quantifiable over 1989-2000 (Table 1). Basis not stated (monitoring results). Annual means 1994-2000 ranged from 0.33 to 0.43 ppm (Figure 1; other years figure-only).

findings.group: young chickens, USDA FSIS National Residue Program, 1994
findings.notes: 95% CI 0.40-0.47 ppm. Mean computed with non-quantifiable results (< 0.20 ppm) set to 0.10 ppm; 30% of young-chicken liver samples were non-quantifiable over 1989-2000 (Table 1). Basis not stated (monitoring results).

findings.group: young chickens, USDA FSIS National Residue Program, 1999
findings.notes: 95% CI 0.30-0.36 ppm. Mean computed with non-quantifiable results (< 0.20 ppm) set to 0.10 ppm; 30% of young-chicken liver samples were non-quantifiable over 1989-2000 (Table 1). Basis not stated (monitoring results).

findings.group: young chickens, USDA FSIS National Residue Program, 2000
findings.notes: 95% CI 0.37-0.41 ppm. Mean computed with non-quantifiable results (< 0.20 ppm) set to 0.10 ppm; 30% of young-chicken liver samples were non-quantifiable over 1989-2000 (Table 1). Basis not stated (monitoring results).

material.label_as_printed: Liver (mature chickens, turkeys, hogs and all other monitored livestock species)

findings.group: annual category means, USDA FSIS National Residue Program, 1994-2000
findings.notes: Range of annual mean values across the four non-young-chicken categories; per-category values figure-only (Figure 1). Non-quantifiable share 74-93% (Table 1), so means are dominated by the 0.10 ppm imputed value.

unresolved: Chicken muscle concentrations (e.g., 0.13 µg/g) are derived from liver values using manufacturer liver-to-muscle ratios (2.9, 4.2, 11), not measured; not recorded as findings.
Inorganic arsenic intake assumes 65% of total arsenic is inorganic; no inorganic arsenic was measured.
Per-year means other than 1994, 1999 and 2000 are figure-only (Figure 1).
The laboratory method, LOD and QA of the NRP analyses are not described.
State-level means (< 0.10 to > 0.51 ppm) are mentioned without data.
Muscle (14), kidney (2) and egg (1) samples were excluded by the authors.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Estimated inorganic arsenic intake at mean chicken consumption (60 g/day), liver-to-muscle ratios 2.9-11
Estimated inorganic arsenic intake at 99th percentile consumption (350 g/day), ratio 2.9
